subject: [PATCH v2 0/3] mm: zswap: free cold writeback folios promptly

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a swap cache folio is still under writeback when it is freed, and requested a defensive check to skip freeing such folios.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti questioned whether the optimization is necessary, pointing out that since we're already in a sleepable context, the folio can be safely dropped from the swap cache here, and sync folios are never handled by the dropbehind workqueue.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Yosry,

On Mon, Jul 27, 2026 at 7:05 PM Yosry Ahmed <yosry@kernel.org> wrote:

---

That's an optimization rather than a real need: since we know we are
in a sleepable context, we can safely drop the folio from the swap
cache here. And since we don't mark the sync folios as dropbehind,
they never enter the list handled by the dropbehind workqueue.

But maybe that's not worth it? I don't even have numbers to back the
optimization claim, so I can drop this in v3.

Thanks,

Alex

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested testing the patch on a different use case, specifically zswap writeback to zram, to see if it improves performance.
reviews.raw_body:
It's a bit artificial, but you can try testing zswap writeback to
zram? :) Likely you'll see some small tput win there?

(TBH I have not seen sync IO swap backends other than zram though so
idk what's more realistic. We don't have pmem device available for
testing etc.)

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed uncertainty about the implications of the patch on synchronous swap backends, specifically mentioning zram, and admitted to only using zswap on zram for testing.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah that's what I'm thinking too, to be completely honest. But my
mental model for sync backend is zram, so I'm not sure if there are
other cases that are interesting that I'm not familiar with.

Normally I just use zswap on zram for correctness stress testing :)
That set up fishes out a surprising amount of bugs.

2026-07-28.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of zswap by allowing it to free cold writeback folios promptly on completion, rather than leaving them for page reclaim. The existing dropbehind mechanism is extended to swap cache folios and zswap is made to opt into this mechanism. This change reduces the number of pages scanned during reclaim and keeps cold memory resident for shorter periods. The patch series includes three patches that move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator, implement dropbehind for swap cache folios, and modify zswap to allocate its writeback folio off the LRU and mark it as dropbehind.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary: Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti agreed to the patch and suggested dropping it into version 3 of the series.
reviews.raw_body:
Ok, I'll drop it in v3 then!

Thanks for your feedback,

Alex

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a swap cache folio is still under writeback when it's being freed, and suggested adding a check to skip freeing the folio in this case.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for your feedback too,

Alex
